gloss: entering a warehouse or garage; receiving into storage; arriving at the depot

definitions.gloss: placing (goods) into a warehouse; receiving stock into storage
definitions.explanation: The arrival or receipt of goods into a warehouse, stockroom, or storage facility — a standard logistics term for inventory coming in. Contrasts with {出庫|しゅっこ} (shipping out of storage).

definitions.gloss: (of a vehicle) pulling into a garage, parking lot, or depot
definitions.explanation: A vehicle entering its garage, depot, or parking space — used of cars entering a parking facility, trains returning to the rail yard, and buses going back to the depot at the end of service.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{商品|しょうひん}が{入庫|にゅうこ}した。
examples.english: The new stock has come in.

examples.japanese: {入庫|にゅうこ}の{予定|よてい}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
{発注|はっちゅう}した{部品|ぶひん}がまだ{入庫|にゅうこ}していないため、{生産|せいさん}ラインが{止|と}まっている。
examples.english: The parts we ordered still haven't arrived in the warehouse, so the production line is halted.

examples.japanese: {最終|さいしゅう}{電車|でんしゃ}が{車庫|しゃこ}に{入庫|にゅうこ}した。
examples.english: The last train pulled into the depot.

examples.japanese: {立体|りったい}{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}に{入庫|にゅうこ}する{際|さい}は、ゆっくり{進|すす}んでください。
examples.english: Please drive slowly when entering the multi-story parking garage.

examples.japanese: バスは{運行|うんこう}{終了後|しゅうりょうご}、{営業所|えいぎょうしょ}に{入庫|にゅうこ}して{点検|てんけん}を{受|う}けます。
examples.english: After its route is finished, the bus pulls into the depot and is given an inspection.

notes:
Composed of {入|にゅう} ("enter") + {庫|こ} ("storehouse, garage"). Literally "entering the storehouse," and applies to both goods going into a warehouse (sense 1) and vehicles going into a garage or depot (sense 2).

USAGE:
- Used as a する-verb ({入庫|にゅうこ}する) and as a plain noun, often in logistics compounds: {入庫|にゅうこ}{日|び} (date of receipt), {入庫|にゅうこ}{数|すう} (number of items received), {入庫|にゅうこ}{予定|よてい} (scheduled arrival).
- Sense 1 is standard in retail, manufacturing, and supply-chain contexts — store staff talk about when stock "comes in," and inventory systems record {入庫|にゅうこ} events.
- Sense 2 is most visible on parking-garage signage and train/bus schedules. The last scheduled service of the day is often described as entering its depot — {車庫|しゃこ}{入庫|にゅうこ} — and late-night trains/buses may be labeled 「{入庫|にゅうこ}」 on destination boards.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Intransitive: stock / a vehicle enters storage — {商品|しょうひん}が{入庫|にゅうこ}する.
- Transitive: to place stock into storage — {入庫|にゅうこ}させる, or in plain form {〜を{入庫|にゅうこ}する} (also widely used in logistics writing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 1):
- {商品|しょうひん}が{入庫|にゅうこ}する: stock comes in
- {入庫|にゅうこ}{予定|よてい}: scheduled inbound
- {入庫|にゅうこ}{日|び}: date of receipt
- {入庫|にゅうこ}{検査|けんさ}: incoming inspection

COMMON COLLOCATIONS (sense 2):
- {駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}に{入庫|にゅうこ}する: to pull into the parking garage
- {車庫|しゃこ}{入庫|にゅうこ}: returning to the depot
- {入庫|にゅうこ}{時間|じかん}: time of entry
- {最終|さいしゅう}{入庫|にゅうこ}: last train/bus to the depot

ANTONYM:
- {出庫|しゅっこ}: shipping out of storage / leaving the garage — the complementary term for both senses.

RELATED TERMS:
- {在庫|ざいこ}: inventory, stock on hand
- {倉庫|そうこ}: warehouse
- {車庫|しゃこ}: garage, depot
- {納品|のうひん}: delivery (of goods to a customer) — the upstream act that precedes {入庫|にゅうこ} on the receiving end
